subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Last Combustion Engine
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Last Combustion Engine usable.

hook.text: The European Union plans to ban new combustion-engine car sales by 2035.

buildup.text: China, California, and several nations announced similar deadlines within the next two decades.

discovery.text: Over a billion combustion cars run on roads today—replacing them will take many decades more.

twist.text: In many developing nations EVs remain too expensive, so combustion engines will last far longer.

climax.text: Some predict the last combustion car will be built around 2060—others say much sooner.

punchline.text: The combustion engine isn't dead yet but its retirement date is set.

quiz.question: When does the EU plan to ban new combustion-only car sales?

details.summary: As electrification accelerates, the last new combustion engine designs are being finalized by automakers planning to end development by 2025 to 2030, marking the twilight of a technology that dominated for over a century.
details.whyItMatters: The end of combustion engine development represents a historic technological transition. It forces an entire industry to redirect engineering talent, manufacturing capacity, and supply chains toward electrification.
takeaways: Most automakers plan to end new engine development by 2025 to 2030
Existing designs will be produced for decades in some markets
Engine engineers are being retrained for electric powertrain roles

faq.question: When will new combustion engines stop being developed?
faq.answer: Mercedes, Volkswagen, and others have announced their last new engine platforms. Most major automakers will stop designing new combustion engines by 2030, though existing designs may be produced for years afterward.

faq.question: Will combustion engines disappear entirely?
faq.answer: Not for decades. Existing cars last 15 to 20 years, and markets without charging infrastructure will need combustion engines longer. Specialty applications like aviation and heavy industry may use combustion engines well beyond 2050.
